texts: Total Loss or Standing Home. Two Different Claims.
You always have final say on any settlement
Total loss: the question is the rebuild number, code upgrades, debris removal, and if your limits are enough.
Standing home: the question is smoke, ash, and whether the house is truly fit to live in.
The builder's question on a total loss.
Can the foundation be reused? That's an engineer's call. Heat damaged concrete and rebar often can't carry a new house, and that decision moves the rebuild number more than almost anything else.

After Washington's August 2023 Gray and Oregon Road fires, 244 of 355 significant dwelling claims paid out their full limits. Once you hit the dwelling limit, the other coverages have to carry the rebuild. Code upgrades. Extended replacement cost. Debris removal.
What California policyholders are owed after a declared state of emergency
Policy terms and limits still apply.
At least 24 months. Up to 12 more if rebuilding is delayed by things beyond your control and you act in good faith.
At least 36 months from the first actual cash value payment to collect it, with extensions of 6 months for good cause.

On a total loss of a furnished primary residence, the insurer must offer at least 60% of the contents limit, up to $350,000, without an itemized inventory (policies issued or renewed from July 1, 2026).
The insurer can't require it sooner than 100 days.
24 months from the start of the loss.
In May 2026 the California Department of Insurance alleged 398 violations in 114 of 220 State Farm wildfire claims its examiners reviewed. These are allegations, not findings.

For homes in a declared catastrophic disaster area, California bars public adjusters from soliciting you until seven days after the event ends. It doesn't apply if you call us first, and then we can look at your claim the same business day.
Call Before the Carrier Sets the Narrative.
Your insurance company has an adjuster protecting their interests. You have the right to one too.
Monday to Friday, 9 AM to 5 PM Pacific
